description: Every component, pattern and block Nowind documents: where its page is, what it is for, when to use it and not, and the classes its examples use; a pattern or block also lists the components (and patterns) it is built from. Examples use regular classes only.

components.name: Button
components.summary: Starts an action. One control height tall, padded by the text edge, with an icon side that steps in by one margin.
use: One primary button per view, for the action most people take.
Wrap the label in a <span>, and put the icon in its own <i> beside it.
avoid: A button for navigation; use a link styled the same way.
Two primary buttons side by side; make the second secondary.

components.name: Icon button
components.summary: A button with only an icon. size-control makes it square and the same height as a text button; size-nested is the small size for inside a toolbar or field.
use: Always give it an aria-label.
size-control on its own; size-nested with icon icon-sm inside a toolbar, field or segmented control.
avoid: An icon whose meaning isn't obvious; add a text label instead.

components.name: Segmented control
components.summary: A set of mutually exclusive options. The pressed segment is styled by aria-pressed, not by a class.
use: Two to five short options that change a view in place.
The box is h-control rounded-sm border-2 border-transparent: the transparent border is its only padding (2px), and the segments are h-full rounded-inner, so their corners follow the box exactly.
Segments touch; the pressed one lifts with pressed:bg-white.
avoid: Options that navigate to another page; use tabs.

components.name: Button group
components.summary: Related buttons in one run, a hairline (gap-px) apart. The outer ends keep the control corner; the corners that face each other drop to the small one, so the run reads as one object.
use: Two to four actions that belong together, such as Undo and Redo.
rounded-s-sm rounded-e-xs on the first, rounded-xs between, rounded-s-xs rounded-e-sm on the last; logical sides, so the run mirrors in right-to-left text.
avoid: A group for options where one is chosen; use a segmented control.

components.name: Split button
components.summary: The usual action and, joined to it, a square key that opens the other ways to do it in a menu. Both halves share a variant; the group has its own name.
use: When one action is the common one and the others are its variations.
Name the key after what it opens (More save options).
avoid: A split button whose menu holds unrelated actions; use an action menu.

components.name: Badge
components.summary: A short label for a status or category, at the nested control size.
use: Pair a status color with its word, never color alone.
avoid: A badge as a button; badges aren't interactive.

components.name: Alert
components.summary: A message about the page or a task, tinted by its status. One line sits in the geometry of a field; a titled alert puts a large icon beside its title and the detail below.
use: One line for a single sentence; a title row with icon-lg when there is detail or an action.
role="status" for information, role="alert" only for errors that need attention now.
avoid: Stacking several alerts; merge them into one.
A large icon on a one-line alert, or the base icon beside a title.

components.name: Toast
components.summary: A brief confirmation on the inverse colours. One line keeps its action inline; a toast with detail stacks title, detail and actions in one text column, with the icon and dismiss on the first line.
use: Confirm an action that already happened, with Undo when it can be reversed.
One line when the message is a few words; title and detail when it needs a second sentence.
avoid: Errors the person must fix; use an alert near the problem.

components.name: Tag
components.summary: A label someone added, at the nested height on a full round, in a neutral, tinted, solid or draft (dashed) face. A removable tag ends in its own small round key.
use: Tags for what people file things under; badges for a status the system sets.
Name each remove key after its tag (Remove Tokens).
avoid: Colour as the only meaning of a tag; the label says it.

components.name: Text field
components.summary: A labelled field built from slots: a leading icon that says what kind of value it takes, a prefix, the input, a suffix and a trailing action. The box is the control; the input inside is bare.
use: A leading icon for the kind of value, so a long form scans by shape.
Prefixes and suffixes for parts the person doesn't type: a scheme, a currency sign, a unit.
gap-2xs between label, box and help; gap-md between fields.
avoid: A placeholder instead of a label.
A unit inside the value ("72.5 kg"): it breaks number keyboards and parsing.
More than one trailing action in a box.

components.name: Select
components.summary: A native select. select-base turns on the customizable select, so the picker takes the theme; a <button> holding <selectedcontent> lets a long value end in an ellipsis instead of wrapping.
use: Five or more options; fewer fit a segmented control or radios.
avoid: Options people need to compare side by side.

components.name: Checkbox, radio and switch
components.summary: Native inputs drawn by the reset at Affine's mark size. A switch is a checkbox with role="switch".
use: A switch for a setting that applies at once; a checkbox for one that waits for Save.
Wrap each one in its label, so the text is part of the target.
avoid: Wrapping inputs in custom elements; the reset styles the native ones.

components.name: Combobox
components.summary: A text field with suggestions, using the native list attribute and a <datalist>.
use: Long lists where typing is faster than scrolling, and free text is allowed.
avoid: A fixed set of five or fewer; use radios or a segmented control.

components.name: Date range
components.summary: Two native date fields grouped as one, with their own labels.
use: Native date inputs: they bring the platform's picker and keyboard support.
avoid: A single text field for both dates.

components.name: Textarea
components.summary: A field for more than one line. It pads like a text field and grows with rows; the help line under it counts down.
use: Set rows to the length you expect; the reset lets people resize it vertically.
Tie the help line to the field with aria-describedby.
avoid: A textarea for one line of text; use a text field.

components.name: Slider
components.summary: A native range input, themed by the reset: track, fill and thumb in the accent. Its value prints beside the label in tabular figures.
use: Print the value next to the label so the slider isn't the only way to read it.
Show the ends of the range when they mean something.
avoid: A slider for an exact number; pair it with a number field or use one.

components.name: Number field
components.summary: A field box with a step button at each end and a bare number input between, so people can type or step.
use: Label each step button with what it does (Fewer seats, More seats), not with minus and plus.
avoid: Step buttons for a value people mostly type, such as a year.

components.name: File upload
components.summary: A drop zone that is a label for a hidden file input, so a click opens the picker and the whole area is the target.
use: Say which files it takes and how large, before anyone tries.
Keep the input in the label (sr-only), so keyboard and screen reader users get the native picker.
avoid: A drop zone with no click fallback.

components.name: Tag input
components.summary: Chips inside a field box, each with its own remove button, then a bare input for the next one.
use: Name each remove button after its chip (Remove design).
Inside a field box the chips take rounded-xs, the nested corner, as a nested select does.
avoid: Chips for a single value; use a select.

components.name: Calendar
components.summary: A month as a seven-column grid of day buttons. The chosen day is aria-pressed, today carries aria-current="date", and days from the next month are quieter.
use: Label each day with the full date, so a screen reader doesn't read a bare number.
Prefer the native date field (see Date range) unless people need to see the month.
avoid: A calendar for a date years away, such as a birthday; let people type it.

components.name: Colour picker
components.summary: The platform colour input as the swatch, a row of presets that are pressed when chosen, and the hue and lightness as labelled sliders with their values printed.
use: The native colour input for the swatch: it brings the platform's picker.
Name each preset by its colour, not its value.
avoid: Colour without a name or value beside it; not everyone can tell the swatches apart.

components.name: One-time code
components.summary: Six square cells in two groups of three, one digit each. A few lines of script move to the next cell as you type, back on Backspace, and spread a pasted or autofilled code across the cells. The first cell takes autocomplete="one-time-code", so a phone offers the code from the message.
use: inputmode="numeric" on every cell, so phones show the number pad.
Without the script the cells still work one by one; the script only moves focus and spreads a paste.
avoid: Clearing every cell on a wrong code; let people fix the digit they got wrong.

components.name: Card
components.summary: A surface that groups related content, padded at the surface level.
use: p-md for padding, the same on every card.
avoid: Cards inside cards; use a divider or a subtle background instead.

components.name: Media card
components.summary: A card led by a 16:9 media area, then a title, a line of detail and its author.
use: aspect-video keeps the media area's shape before the image loads.
@container on the wrapper lets the card lay itself out by its own width: @md:flex-row puts the media beside the text once the card is 448px wide, wherever it sits.
avoid: Text over the image without a scrim.

components.name: Tabs
components.summary: Switches between views of the same thing. The selected tab is styled by aria-selected.
use: Moving aria-selected is all the script a tab needs for its look.
avoid: More than six tabs; use a sidebar.

components.name: Breadcrumbs
components.summary: Shows where a page sits in the hierarchy.
use: Three or more levels deep.
avoid: Repeating the page title right below it.

components.name: Pagination
components.summary: Moves through pages of results. The current page is styled by aria-current.
use: Long lists where people jump to a page; show the total near it.
avoid: Feeds people scroll through; load more instead.

components.name: Sidebar navigation
components.summary: A column of links at the control height, each an icon and a label. aria-current="page" marks where you are, and current: paints it.
use: In an app shell, w-sidebar gives it the shell's sidebar width.
A count sits at the end of its row, in a small round marker.
avoid: More than about eight links without a heading between groups.

components.name: Navbar
components.summary: The app's top bar: a wordmark, the main links, then actions at the end. Below lg the links move into a menu behind a button at the start.
use: In an app shell give it h-header, and keep its content on one line: that is the height the rest of the shell assumes.
The same links twice: hidden lg:flex in the bar, and in a popover behind a lg:hidden menu button.
avoid: More than one primary action in the bar.

components.name: Steps
components.summary: A numbered row of the steps in a task: done steps show a check, the current one carries aria-current="step", and a rule joins each to the next.
use: Three to five steps; name each by what it collects.
avoid: Steps for a single form people fill in one go.

components.name: Tree
components.summary: Folders as <details>, each a row at the control height whose caret turns when it opens, and its files indented one step. aria-current="page" marks the open file.
use: One level of folders; deeper trees need a script for the arrow keys a tree role promises.
avoid: A tree for fewer than a dozen items; a list is quicker to scan.

components.name: Popover menu
components.summary: A menu that opens with popovertarget and sits against its button with anchor-bottom. No script.
use: Put layout classes such as flex on an inner element: on the popover itself they would keep it visible when closed.
avoid: A menu for the page's main navigation.

components.name: Dialog
components.summary: A modal <dialog> opened with the command attribute; the reset dims the page behind it.
use: m-auto centers it; the reset zeroes margins.
Confirm destructive actions with the action's own word, not OK.
avoid: Dialogs that open on page load.

components.name: Tooltip
components.summary: A hint that shows when its trigger is hovered or focused. The wrapper is a group; the hint uses group-hover: and group-focus-within:. No script.
use: A short label for an icon-only button, also given as its aria-label.
group-focus-within: as well as group-hover:, so keyboard users see it.
avoid: Anything people need to read to finish a task; put it on the page.

components.name: Drawer
components.summary: A modal <dialog> that sits against the end edge, opened with command. For filters and settings that work on the page behind it.
use: ms-auto pushes it to the end edge; my-xs me-xs keep it off the window's edges.
avoid: A drawer for a short confirmation; use a dialog.

components.name: Action menu
components.summary: The actions for one item, behind an icon button: a role="menu" popover with a rule between groups and the destructive action last, in the danger colour. A script can open the same menu on right-click with showPopover().
use: Name the button after its item (Actions for Q3 report), since its icon says nothing.
Put the destructive action last, after a rule.
avoid: An action menu for the one action most people take; show that as a button.

components.name: Popover card
components.summary: A preview of a person or a thing, opened from its name with popovertarget and placed with anchor-bottom. A hover card is the same card, shown by a script on hover and focus.
use: Facts that help people decide whether to open the full page.
avoid: Anything people need to finish a task; a card that only shows on hover is easy to miss.

components.name: Command palette
components.summary: A search field over grouped results, one line each, with the active result aria-selected and the keys in a footer. Shown here in place; on a page it is a modal <dialog> opened with ⌘K.
use: Group results by kind, and keep each to one line.
Keep focus in the field and move the selection with aria-activedescendant.
avoid: A palette as the only way to reach a command; it is a shortcut, not the menu.

components.name: Accordion
components.summary: Sections that open and close, built from <details>.
use: list-none on the summary hides the marker, including Safari's.
avoid: Hiding content most people need; show it.

components.name: Avatar and group
components.summary: Initials on an accent solid, one control height square; a group overlaps them.
use: A border in the page color separates overlapping avatars.
avoid: More than five in a row; end with a count.

components.name: Progress bar
components.summary: Native progress and meter, themed by the reset, or a track and a fill sized with a fraction class.
use: Always print the value next to the bar.
progress for a task under way; meter for a level within a range, which turns warning or danger past its high and low.
avoid: A bar for something that isn't a share of a whole.

components.name: Table
components.summary: Rows of records in a surface that scrolls sideways on narrow screens.
use: font-mono tabular-nums for figures so columns line up.
avoid: A table for layout.

components.name: Sortable table
components.summary: Column headers hold buttons; aria-sort on the header says which column sorts the rows and in which order.
use: Show the sort direction with an icon and in aria-sort.
Sorting itself is a script's job; the classes only show the state.
avoid: Sorting columns nobody compares.

components.name: Description list
components.summary: Terms and their values in a <dl>: one column on a phone, the term beside its value from sm up.
use: Read-only facts about one thing: an account, an order, a file.
avoid: A description list for data people compare across rows; use a table.

components.name: Stat
components.summary: One figure in a card: what it counts, the value in tabular figures, and how it moved.
use: Say what the change compares against.
Put the direction in an icon as well as the colour.
avoid: More than four stats in a row; people stop reading them.

components.name: Timeline
components.summary: Events in order down a rule: a small round marker for each, its title and when it happened.
use: Newest first, unless the order of steps matters more than recency.
avoid: A timeline for events people need to filter or sort; use a table.

components.name: Code block
components.summary: A <figure> with a caption naming the file and a copy button, over a <pre> that scrolls sideways rather than wrap.
use: Name the file or language in the caption.
Let long lines scroll (overflow-x-auto) so the code keeps its shape.
avoid: Wrapping code lines; it changes what the code looks like.

components.name: Keyboard key
components.summary: A key in running text, at the nested height with the keycap's padding and corner, set in the mono face.
use: One <kbd> per key, a space between the keys of a shortcut.
avoid: Keycaps for words that aren't keys.

components.name: Rich text
components.summary: Formatted prose, such as rendered Markdown or an agent's answer: a heading, paragraphs, a list, a quote and code, each block a step apart in one column at a readable measure.
use: One column, gap-sm between blocks, at max-w-text.
Let code scroll sideways rather than wrap.
avoid: Headings larger than the page's own; rich text sits inside a page.

components.name: Empty state
components.summary: What a view shows before it has content, with the action that fills it.
use: Say what will appear here and how to start.
avoid: Jokes or illustrations that hide the action.

components.name: Spinner and skeleton
components.summary: animate-spin for a short wait, animate-pulse placeholders for content that's on its way.
use: Shape skeletons like the content that replaces them.
avoid: A spinner for a wait longer than a few seconds; show progress.

components.name: Banner
components.summary: A message across the top of a page or region, on the accent's solid with its contrast text, and one link.
use: One banner at a time, for news that concerns everyone on the page.
avoid: A banner for an error in a form; put that next to the field.

components.name: Callout
components.summary: A note set apart from the text around it by a start rule and a soft fill, with a title and its detail.
use: Asides in long text: a tip, a caveat, a note on an older version.
avoid: A callout for a status the reader must act on; use an alert.

components.name: Response actions
components.summary: The row under a generated answer: copy, helpful and not helpful as pressed toggles, retry, the version switcher, then a quiet line of when and how long.
use: Helpful and Not helpful as aria-pressed toggles; pressing again clears it.
Disable Previous and Next at the ends; hide the switcher with one version.
avoid: Labels on every action; the icons are common enough, and each has an aria-label.

components.name: Trace
components.summary: What an agent did, one step to a row: a round mark for its state (done, running, waiting, failed), its name, its time or status, and the detail behind a <details>. A rule joins each mark to the next: solid after a finished step, dashed after one still to come.
use: Each row's aria-label joins the name and the state, so it reads as one.
Open the running step, closed the rest.
avoid: The trace instead of the answer; it explains how, the answer says what.

components.name: Composer
components.summary: A message box: context chips, a text area that grows with what is typed (field-sizing-content), then one row with Attach at the start and, at the end, the model as a quiet text trigger and one round key at the full control size: Dictate while the box is empty, Send once something is typed (a few lines of script swap their hidden).
use: A <form>, so Enter and the Send button submit without a script.
Name Send and Stop in aria-label; they are icons.
avoid: A placeholder as the only label.

patterns.name: Sign in
patterns.summary: The first step of signing in: the providers as full-width buttons, a rule, then an email field and Continue. A link to create an account sits in the lead, single sign-on at the foot.
use: Ask for the email first; the next step depends on it (password, code or single sign-on).
Set autocomplete on every field.
avoid: Asking for the password on the same screen as the providers.

patterns.name: Sign in with a password
patterns.summary: The second step: who is signing in, with a way back, the password field with a key to show it, and the other ways in below.
use: Show the email being signed in, with a link back to change it.
A show key with aria-pressed, so people can check what they typed.
avoid: Saying whether the email or the password was wrong; say they don't match.

patterns.name: Sign-in code
patterns.summary: A code sent by email: six cells that the platform can fill from the message, the address it went to, and a way to send another.
use: The one-time code component: six cells, the first with autocomplete="one-time-code", so phones offer the code from the message.
Pause the resend link for a while after each send, and say for how long.
avoid: Six cells without the script that spreads a paste across them.

patterns.name: Create account
patterns.summary: The first step of signing up, built like sign-in: what the plan costs in the lead, the providers, then the work email and Continue.
use: Say what it costs before anyone types.
avoid: Asking for name and password before the email is checked.

patterns.name: Account details
patterns.summary: The second step of signing up: name and a new password, with a strength meter as the password's help line, and a way to skip the password.
use: autocomplete="new-password", so password managers offer to make one.
Say what would make the password stronger, not only that it is weak.
avoid: A second field to repeat the password; the show key does the job.

patterns.name: Verify email
patterns.summary: The last step of signing up: the code sent to the new address, how long it lasts, and a way to change the address.
use: Say when the code expires.
avoid: Locking the account after one wrong code.

patterns.name: Joined workspace
patterns.summary: Where an invitation ends: who is already there as a group of avatars, the workspace and your role, and one button to go in.
use: Show who is already there; it says the invitation was real.
avoid: A tour before people reach the workspace.

patterns.name: Settings section
patterns.summary: A titled group of settings, one per row: what it does on the left, its control on the right, a rule between rows. On a phone each row stacks.
use: Name each control after its row (aria-label), since the row's text is not its label.
Switches take effect at once; keep Save for settings that wait for it.
avoid: A switch and a Save button for the same setting.

patterns.name: Filter bar
patterns.summary: A search field that takes the free width, a segmented control for the view, and the count of what is shown, above the list it filters.
use: Say how many of how many are shown, in a role="status" line, so the change is announced.
avoid: More than three filters in the bar; move the rest behind a Filters button.

patterns.name: Member list
patterns.summary: People one to a row: avatar, name and a supporting line, a role badge, and the row's actions behind one icon button at the end.
use: Truncate the name and the supporting line, so the badge and actions stay on the row.
avoid: A row of action buttons on every person; one menu keeps the list scannable.

patterns.name: No results
patterns.summary: A search that found nothing: the query stays in the field, and the empty state says what was searched and offers one way out.
use: Repeat the query in the message, so people see what they typed.
avoid: Clearing the field when nothing is found.

patterns.name: Notification list
patterns.summary: A panel of notifications, newest first: an unread one carries a dot at the end, labelled for screen readers, and one action marks them all read.
use: Give the unread dot its own label, so the state is not colour alone.
avoid: Notifications people must act on; send those to the page they concern.

patterns.name: Confirm delete
patterns.summary: The body of a dialog for an action that can't be undone: what will go, a field that asks for the name, and the danger button last. Shown here in place of the dialog.
use: Name the thing and say what goes with it.
Ask for the name only where a mistake is costly; one confirm is enough elsewhere.
avoid: A confirm dialog for an action that can be undone; offer Undo in a toast instead.

patterns.name: Pricing
patterns.summary: Plans side by side from lg up, each a card with a price in tabular figures, what it includes and its own button. The recommended plan takes the accent border.
use: Three plans at most, with the one most people should pick in the middle.
avoid: A feature list that differs only in numbers; put those in a comparison table.

patterns.name: Comment thread
patterns.summary: Comments oldest first, each an avatar, a name with when it was written, and the text; the reply box last, where the thread ends.
use: Times relative while recent, a date once older than a week.
avoid: Nesting replies more than one level; long threads read better flat.

patterns.name: Page header
patterns.summary: Where the page sits, its title and one supporting line, with the page's actions at the end of the title row; on a phone the actions wrap under the title.
use: One primary action; the rest in secondary buttons or the menu.
avoid: Breadcrumbs on a page one level down; the back link is enough.

patterns.name: Bulk actions
patterns.summary: A table with a checkbox on each row. While rows are selected a bar across the top of the table says how many, and holds what can be done to all of them.
use: Put the count in a role="status" line, so it is announced as it changes.
A select-all checkbox in the header.
avoid: Showing the bar before anything is selected.

patterns.name: Details panel
patterns.summary: One record's facts in a card: its name and status, then terms and values that stack on a phone and sit side by side from sm up.
use: Status at the top, next to the name, where it is read first.
avoid: Editing in place in a details panel; open a form.

patterns.name: Onboarding checklist
patterns.summary: The first things to do, with how far along you are: done steps checked and struck through, the next one with its button.
use: Three to five steps, each finished by one action.
avoid: Hiding the product until the list is done.

patterns.name: Upload list
patterns.summary: Files below the drop zone, one to a row: a bar while uploading with a way to cancel, the size once done, and the reason and a retry when it fails.
use: Say why an upload failed, next to the file.
avoid: One bar for the whole batch; people need to see which file is stuck.

patterns.name: Invite form
patterns.summary: An email field and a role on one row from sm up, the button at the end, and a line on what the role can do.
use: Default the role to the one most people get.
avoid: Asking for a name; the person adds it when they join.

patterns.name: FAQ
patterns.summary: Questions as an accordion under a title, the first answer open, and a way to ask something the list doesn't cover.
use: Questions in the words people ask them.
avoid: An FAQ for things the product should explain where they happen.

patterns.name: Feature grid
patterns.summary: What a product does, three to a row from lg up: an icon in a tinted square, a title and one sentence each.
use: One sentence per feature, about what it does for the reader.
avoid: More than six features; the rest belong on their own page.

patterns.name: Newsletter sign-up
patterns.summary: A title, what people get and how often, and an email field that holds its own Subscribe button, at the small size in the field's trailing slot.
use: Say how often, so people know what they agree to.
avoid: Asking for more than an email.

patterns.name: Agent session
patterns.summary: A conversation with an agent in one card: a header with the thread choice, the messages (yours at the end edge on the accent, the agent's as rich text with its trace and actions), and the composer last.
use: The messages in a role="log", so new ones are announced.
Actions only on the latest finished answer.
avoid: Bubbles for the agent's long answers; they read better as plain text the width of the column.

patterns.name: Floating agent session
patterns.summary: A round launcher that opens the chat as a popover over the page: a title bar with minimise and expand, the conversation, and the composer. The same draft stays when it closes.
use: A popover opened by popovertarget: it closes on Escape and outside clicks, with no script.
Keep the draft when the panel closes.
avoid: Covering the page's own primary action with the launcher.

patterns.name: Connections
patterns.summary: The services an account is linked to, one per row: the service's mark with a check on its corner once connected, its name and state, and one action, Use or Connect.
use: Say the state in words as well as with the check; the check is aria-hidden.
The primary button only where something is still to do (Connect).
avoid: Disconnecting from this list without a confirm; put that in the service's settings.

blocks.name: Hero
blocks.summary: The top of a landing page: a kicker, a headline at the display size, one sentence of what it is, and two actions, the primary first. Centred, at a readable measure.
use: One headline and one sentence; the rest of the page explains.
The primary action first, the secondary beside it.
avoid: A carousel of headlines; people read the first.

blocks.name: Feature section
blocks.summary: A section heading with a kicker and a lead, then the feature grid under it.
use: Lead with what the reader gets, not with what the product has.
avoid: A feature section with no heading; the grid alone doesn't say why.

blocks.name: Stats band
blocks.summary: Three or four figures in a row of cards from md up, each with what it counts and how it moved.
use: Figures people can check, with what they count.
avoid: More than four figures; the band stops being read.

blocks.name: Testimonials
blocks.summary: Quotes from people who use it, each a card with the quote and who said it, side by side from md up.
use: A name and a role with every quote.
avoid: Quotes nobody said.

blocks.name: Call to action
blocks.summary: The last section of a landing page, on the accent's solid: one line of what to do, one sentence of why, and the action.
use: The same action as the hero's primary.
avoid: A second, different action here; the page has asked once.

blocks.name: Pricing section
blocks.summary: A centred heading and lead over the plans, and a line under them for anything a plan doesn't answer.
use: Prices in the reader's currency, with what the price is per.
avoid: Hiding the price behind a contact form for every plan.

blocks.name: Site footer
blocks.summary: The foot of every page: the wordmark and one line, columns of links that stack on a phone, and a last row with the year and the legal links.
use: The same footer on every page.
Column titles as small labels, not headings.
avoid: Links people need often; those belong in the header.

blocks.name: App shell
blocks.summary: The frame of an app: the navbar across the top, the sidebar from md up, and the page in the rest, starting with its header.
use: In a real app give the bar h-header and the sidebar w-sidebar, the shell's own lengths.
Below md move the sidebar's links into a menu in the bar.
avoid: A second sidebar on the other side; put that detail in a drawer.

blocks.name: Dashboard
blocks.summary: A page header, a row of figures, then the table the figures summarise, with a link to see all of it.
use: Figures first, then the rows behind them.
avoid: Charts for a single number; the figure is clearer.
